rules.label: Vegetable and fruit peels
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Organic kitchen scrap decomposes naturally into nutrient-rich compost.

rules.label: Cooked food, rice, dal, leftovers
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Cooked kitchen leftovers are biodegradable and suitable for composting or biogas.

rules.label: Meat and fish scraps
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Raw and cooked animal scraps decompose organically in municipal compost streams.

rules.label: Large bones
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Bones are biodegradable organic matter, though some local compost facilities reject them.

rules.label: Egg shells
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Eggshells are mineral-rich organic material that enriches municipal compost.

rules.label: Tea leaves, coffee grounds
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Used beverage grounds decompose rapidly; remove any plastic pyramid bags beforehand.

rules.label: Flowers, pooja offerings
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Floral and pooja offerings are compostable organic plant material.

rules.label: Garden trimmings, dry leaves
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Foliage and plant prunings decompose into organic mulch; keep separated from recyclables.

rules.label: Coconut shell
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Hard shells are organic, but slow degradation causes some cities to sort them dry.

rules.label: Used cooking oil
rules.action: Seal it in a bottle and check municipal guidance.
rules.reason: Liquid fats clog drains and disrupt composting; separate municipal collection guidelines apply.
rules.guidance: The rules don't clearly cover this. Seal it in a bottle and ask your local body how to dispose of it.

rules.label: Spoiled packaged food (contents)
rules.action: Put it in the wet (compost) bin.
rules.reason: Empty food contents into organic waste and place outer packaging in dry recycling.

rules.label: Newspaper, paper, cardboard
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Clean paper and cardboard fibers are valuable feedstocks for domestic paper recycling mills.

rules.label: Plastic bottles (PET), jugs
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Clean polyethylene terephthalate bottles are mechanically recycled into new polymer products.

rules.label: Milk pouches, carry bags
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Low-density polyethylene film can be reprocessed into recycled plastic granules.

rules.label: Chips and biscuit wrappers (multilayer plastic)
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Multilayer packaging is collected under extended producer responsibility for energy recovery.

rules.label: Tetra pak cartons
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Aseptic composite cartons are processed at specialized paper pulp recovery units.

rules.label: Thermocol (EPS)
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Expanded polystyrene packaging is classified as dry, though local recycling access varies.

rules.label: Glass bottles and jars
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Intact glassware is infinitely recyclable when segregated free of contamination.

rules.label: Broken glass
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Broken glass belongs in dry waste but must be wrapped to prevent sanitation worker injuries.

rules.label: Broken crockery, ceramics
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Ceramics cannot be melted like glass; wrap sharp fragments before dry disposal.

rules.label: Metal cans, tins, utensils
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Aluminium, tin, and steel scrap are high-value dry recyclables with mature reprocessing chains.

rules.label: Aluminium foil
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Clean foil scrap is remelted into secondary aluminium; shake off food particles.

rules.label: Old clothes, textiles
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Discarded fabric scraps and worn garments are sorted dry for fiber shredding or reuse.

rules.label: Footwear, leather, rubber
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Non-biodegradable shoes and synthetic rubber items are directed to industrial energy recovery.

rules.label: Wood, furniture scraps
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Treated wood, plywood pieces, and small wooden furniture scraps are collected with dry combustibles.

rules.label: Books, magazines
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Paperback books, notebooks, and print periodicals are prime dry recyclables.

rules.label: Plastic cutlery, straws, cups
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Disposable rigid plastics belong in dry recyclables despite challenging mechanical recovery.

rules.label: Paper cups, plates
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Poly-lined paper foodware belongs in dry waste for thermal or specialized fiber extraction.

rules.label: Greasy pizza box
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Corrugated cardboard boxes are collected dry; scrape off leftover crusts and cheese.

rules.label: Bubble wrap, packaging film
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Flexible packaging films and air cushioning wrap are dry recyclable polyethylenes.

rules.label: Plastic toys (no electronics)
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Molded plastic toys without electronic circuitry or batteries belong in general dry recyclables.

rules.label: Used tissue and paper napkins
rules.action: Check hygiene use to select container.
rules.reason: Sanitary contamination determines whether tissue belongs in dry or sanitary containment.

followUp.question: Was it used for blood or bodily fluids?

rules.label: Cigarette butts
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Cellulose acetate filters do not biodegrade rapidly and belong in residual dry waste.

rules.label: Dust, sweepings, ash
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Inert floor sweepings and fireplace ash belong in the non-biodegradable residual dry stream.

rules.label: Empty cosmetic bottles, tubes
rules.action: Put it in the dry bin; rinse if dirty.
rules.reason: Empty cosmetic tubes are dry recyclables; leftover nail polish requires special-care disposal.

rules.label: Diapers (baby and adult)
rules.action: Wrap it securely and keep it in the sanitary waste container.
rules.reason: Soiled diapers contain pathogenic biological material requiring dedicated sanitary disposal.

rules.label: Sanitary pads, tampons
rules.action: Wrap it securely and keep it in the sanitary waste container.
rules.reason: Used menstrual hygiene products must be wrapped securely in paper before disposal.

rules.label: Condoms
rules.action: Wrap it securely and keep it in the sanitary waste container.
rules.reason: Latex prophylaxis contains personal body fluid and must be wrapped for sanitary handling.

rules.label: Wet wipes
rules.action: Wrap it securely and keep it in the sanitary waste container.
rules.reason: Synthetic fiber wipes do not decompose and carry bodily residues requiring sanitary handling.

rules.label: Used bandages, plasters, cotton
rules.action: Check degree of fluid saturation to select container.
rules.reason: Level of biological fluid saturation distinguishes sanitary handling from special-care hazard.

followUp.question: Is it soaked with blood or body fluids?

rules.label: CFL, tube lights
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Fluorescent lamps contain toxic mercury vapor requiring isolated hazardous handling.

rules.label: LED bulbs
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Solid-state lamps contain integrated circuit boards governed by electronic waste management.

rules.label: AA/AAA and button-cell batteries
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Dry electrochemical cells contain heavy metals governed under Battery Waste Management Rules.

rules.label: Phone, power-bank, lithium batteries
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Lithium-ion cells present severe combustion hazards and require authorized battery recyclers.

rules.label: Expired or unused medicines
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Pharmaceuticals can contaminate municipal water supplies and require domestic hazardous disposal.

rules.label: Paint cans, thinners
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Solvent vapors and synthetic pigments are volatile domestic hazardous substances.

rules.label: Pesticide, insecticide, mosquito-repellent containers
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Toxic agrochemical and repellent residues are hazardous domestic chemical wastes.

rules.label: Mercury thermometer
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Liquid elemental mercury is extremely neurotoxic and requires specialized hazardous recovery.

rules.label: Used needles, syringes (home)
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Medical sharps pose serious puncture injury and infection risks to sanitation workers.

rules.label: Contaminated gauze
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Heavily bio-contaminated wound dressings carry infectious pathogen transmission risks.

rules.label: Phones, chargers, cables, small electronics
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Consumer electronics contain recoverable precious metals governed under E-Waste Rules.

rules.label: Printer cartridges
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Toner microparticles and printer electrical components require authorized e-waste collection.

rules.label: Cleaning chemical (acid, phenyl) containers
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Corrosive acid and phenyl residues can burn handlers and damage waste facilities.

rules.label: Razor blades
rules.action: Keep it separate and hand it to a designated collection point.
rules.reason: Exposed sharp steel blades cause severe lacerations to manual waste segregators.

rules.label: Aerosol cans
rules.action: Check if pressurized contents remain.
rules.reason: Pressurized propellants pose explosion risks if crushed before complete emptying.
